dossier.public_summary: The 1.8-Earth-radius dip is unstable: it almost disappears in some TESS sectors/transits and is dominated by a handful of very deep outliers. It shows a second dip half an orbit away and odd/even depth differences that match an eclipsing star, not a planet. With a nearby star capable of causing it and no reliable on-target centroid, a blended eclipsing binary best explains the data.

reasons.why: Depth changes dramatically between sectors and within the same pipeline.
Change is not a calibration offset between products but intrinsic to the SPOC data themselves.
Most signal comes from a few huge, highly significant outliers while several transits show no dip or negative depth, inconsistent with a stable planet transit.
reasons.value: 24 transits, p_consistent 7.93599505765396e-94, share_of_top_3 0.833, outliers 3112 ppm (14.9 sigma), 2133 ppm (9.4 sigma), 2620 ppm (8.2 sigma), -307 ppm (-4.7 sigma)

reasons.why: A second dip with SNR comparable to the strongest brightening and ~30% of the transit depth at phase ~0.55 points to a stellar companion eclipse, not a planet.
reasons.value: snr 6.337 at phase 0.548, depth_ppm 150.2, depth_over_dip 0.309, best_brightening_snr 6.466, secondary_over_bump 0.9801

reasons.why: Odd/Even depths differ substantially (363.9 vs 558.4 ppm), supporting binary interpretation, with sector_oe_max_sigma 6.611 observed.
A catalogued star within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can reproduce the dip with a ~16% eclipse, and centroid is inconclusive, so a blended EB on a neighbour is viable.
reasons.value: could_cause_within_1px 1, plausible_within_1px 1, closest sep 4.3 arcsec delta_mag 6.28 eclipse_needed 0.1612

reasons.why: ML planet score is well below median planet (0.5) near the false-positive regime, consistent with other indicators.
